Total score  75.47/100  (mean 70.26/100)
(Scheme 1 -- 52% final exam + 40% all 5 quizzes + 8% problem sets)

Final grade: B

I flunked out in one of the quiz (greatly below mean!!!) because I used the wrong way for studying. Even though I got 18/20 for most quizzes thereafter, eventually I could only get the total quiz result close to the mean score. For the final exam, the TAs marked the paper more vigorously than I expect. Even if you express the same meaning but without the key words they want, you would end up losing some points or even get a 0 score!!! My result of final exam was slightly lower than my expectation because of that. I am a little bit disappointed for not getting a B+ (I guess a ~80% is needed for a B+). Though, learning Economics is great!
sections.workload: This is only an introductory Economics course without vigorous Maths proofs. Only graphical illustrations and simple Maths representations are required. Without perplexing Maths (like multivariable calculus, econometrics......), workload should not be huge -- even people not sensitive to figures (who flunked out in Accounting course like me) should perform satisfactorily in this course. What you need to do before final exam is to summarize all graphs and concepts once, then try to express in words the logic behind and see how concepts and topics could be connected together. Don't forget to review the quizzes and the practice problems provided on Canvas as well.

sections.content:
Overall, the content in the beginning seems quite similar to IB Economics HL. However, as you move on passing midterms, the key content (that will be tested in the finals) will be significantly different from the IB syllabus such as indifference curve, groves-clarke mechanism, etc.

It may be fine to skip class in the beginning of the semester is you are confident with your knowledge from IB but you may be risking some key contents that IB never touched on and that will be hard to self-study.
sections.teaching:
This is Professor Neary's first year teaching this course, so in view of that, it was quite good. While he may stutter a bit during lectures, he delivers the content quite well and is always willing to listen to students feedback and answer their questions.

He also uses interactive games in class to highlight certain material especially during the game theory sections of the syllabus.
sections.grading:
Professor Neary is considerably lenient in his grading and assessments. The homework (10% of final grade) is often the hardest and if you understand the homework, you will more than likely score well in the finals and mid-terms.

In terms of level of difficulty, it goes by this:
Lecture content<Mid-terms/Finals<Homework

Understanding the homework will definitely help in the exams and the Professor and TA often goes through the homework to ensure students' understanding.
sections.workload: The workload is a bit heavier not in terms of quantity but level of difficulty. The homework often includes content that has not been touched in class yet so it will take time to further research about it. Nonetheless, understanding the homework will really help in your general understanding of economics and the course.

sections.content: This a a economic course designed for students who have studied economics before in their high school.  Actually more than half of the content is covered in the HKDSE syllabus.  Therefore if you don't pay attention in class, do not do any revision, you should not fail.  But of course if you are aiming A range please work hard.  Professor Lim do not take attendance and you can swap freely between his classes, ie if you sleep late or due to other reasons you miss your class, you can still take the other one.  I quite appreciate this flexibility offered by Professor Lim.
sections.teaching: Professor Lim's teaching content is acceptable.  Nothing special.  If you are interested in economics, you will understand more easily.  On the other hand, he also tell jokes in class.  This keeps the atmosphere not too boring.  He also tells stories about his family and himself.  Overall good teaching.
sections.grading: Professor Lim is the only professor who tells me the exact grading curve in this semester.  Top 20% A range, the following 40% B range.  That means if you are just below mean, you still got a B-.  This is already a very "good" grade in ust.  Mid term 35%, final 45%, homework 20%.  So please do not "all in" final.  You will definitely regret if you do not study hard in mid term.  You don't have a chance to get an A if your mid term is bad.
sections.workload: No project, no reading, just have 4-5 homework sets in the whole semester.  Each homework set contains about 5 question.  Most importantly, you can form a group of 5 to do the homework.  One submission per group is required.  That means you actually just need to do 1 question per homework set.  In my point of view, this workload is light.

sections.content: The first half of the course should be simple for most of the students, as they are only about DSE econ stuff. So basically you can skip all lessons before first mid-term exam. However, you need to pay attention into some new concepts that are not included in the DSE econ. For example, budget line, indifference curve etc.
sections.teaching: Her teaching is nothing special at all. I mean, if you are willing to pay effort to read the notes yourself, you need not attend her lessons. During lecture, she just add some extra stuff/ explanations which are not going to be covered in the mid-term/final.
sections.grading:
Personally I think the grading system of this course is quite tough. Take myself as an example. I have 86% in 1st mid-term (median for 1st mid-term); 91% in 2nd mid-term (above mean for around 1 sd); 95.5% in the final exam (above mean for more than 1 sd); completed all quizzes; 1 problem set got full mark , another one got 90% (because of careless)
My overall score for this course is 94.55%, but I can only receive an A- in this course. So if you really want to get a good grade, remember avoid careless mistakes and complete all items as good as possible!
sections.workload:
The workload is light compared with other courses.
Only a few items:
1. 10 online quizzes (credited by hand-in)
2. two problem sets (5% each)
3. two mid-term tests (2 grading system, 40% for counting both: one is counting both mid-term; 30% for counting one: another one is counting one mid-term only) she will choose the one which can generate higher score for you, so you should attend both mid-term tests
4. Final exam (weighted 40/50%, depends on which mid-term calculation approach you have adopted)

sections.content:
Very fundamental Economics. The course starts from NSS Economics (which all local ECON2113 students should have good grasps on it), and then develops into Utility & Demand, Cost and Output, Market Types (perfect competition, monopoly, oligopoly)

The first 40% of course is very easy to everyone. However, difficulties will escalate afterwards and regular practices on questions are very important (The part on utility, indifference curve analysis is the most difficult part because it was an untaught topic in HKDSE but appeared in HKALE)
sections.teaching:
Her teaching is quite boring because she just reads  the Powerpoint slides and add some notes on it. Although it is boring, your concepts will be very clear if you can tolerate that boredom and strive through the semester.

She will assess some side-concepts (but difficult) mentioned in class. For mid-term 2, she assessed the concept that was taught for a few minutes in class (Indifference curve analysis involving Inferior goods). Attend her lessons if you can.
sections.grading:
I get an A in this course. Thanks Wenwen!

The examinations are so simple, very simple that even HKCEE Examination is more difficult (even the same for final examination). Careless mistakes are too FATAL that can kill your grade. I don't support this way of assessment because it fails to categorise able, hard-working students and lazy students effectively. The paper should be set more difficult.

I get 95% finally (95.7% also A). I have heard that cut-off for A+ is 96%. From UST FYS Secret, I hear that some students get B-range for >90% (not completely assured).

During the class, she would invite students to come out and perform activities that facilitate her teaching. This will add 2 credits to your final examination. It is VERY VERY VERY important that it can boost your sub-grade by 1 level. I strongly recommend those who enrol to her course do at least 1 along the semester!
sections.workload:
Workload is light.

You don't need to attend the tutorial. I attended two and three and skipped the remaining.

There are 2 problem sets in the whole semester - Remember to finish them properly with 100% effort. The reason why I cannot get A+ is because i didn't finish the problem set very seriously.

sections.content: The contents of her powerpoints are great with a lot of details, you can easily understand what the theories are talking about. You can also get a high marks through reading her powerpoints. There are 14 microeconomics topic in the whole semester. Most of them are the topics which taught in the DSE syllabus including externalities, short run long run, efficiency and equity, etc. It is easy to handle them if you have studied economics in your DSE.
sections.teaching: Her teaching is nice and she always explains the   economics theories through games and activities. Also, there are no attendance system for her classes. Therefore, you can either attend her classes or absent from her classes, no punishment will be given. However, In my semester, there are 2 points for people who have answer her questions in the lecture.Tutorials are also available. There are useful notes provided in the tutorial classes, which is more important than attending the lecture.
sections.grading: You can easily get a high marks in the exam if you have written relevant concepts in the paper. However, The curve is very high. A range is about 90 something%. You may able to get a A by earning nearly full marks of the mid-term exam and final exam. For the mid term exams, you may either attend both mid terms exams or just attend one exams. There are two grading systems: 1. 20% each for the two mid term exams and 40% for the final exam; 2. 30% for one of the mid term exams and 50% for the final exam. The teacher assistant will help you to use one of the methods to calculate your final scores. So you no need to worry whether you should attend one of the mid terms or atend both mid term exams.
sections.workload: The wokrload is not very high. There are 10 online quizzes with 10 mc questions each and 2 problem set questions within 20 questions each in the semesters. As for the quizzes, participation marks will be given no matter what your scores are. For the problem set questions, most of them can be either found in the textbooks or in the websites. Therefore, you may find many sources and you no need to do by yourself.

sections.content: ECON 2113 is an economics course for students with some econ. background. Part of the content was already covered in HKDSE syllabus, such as opportunity cost, demand/supply, elasticity, government intervention and production possibilities - these were mostly covered before the first mid-term. After the first mid-term the difficulty of the content has increased a lot - indifference curves, long-run/short-run production, oligopoly games, etc. We might have some basic ideas on these topics in HKDSE but they would be discussed in a more in-depth manner in this course.
sections.teaching:
I cannot say Prof. Ding's teaching is useless - she does help me to clear some misunderstandings on the concepts. But her speaking tone is pretty boring and flat, making me fall asleep very often... anyway attendance is not compulsory, just skip the lectures if you can understand the content and dislike her voice.
TA is Peter. He usually covers useful mathematical approaches for solving problems in tutorials, which the problems will appear in the exams. I think it is good for you to attend the tutorials, or at least take a hard-copy of the tutorial notes.
Both Prof. Ding and Peter welcome questions. They are quite patient to answer you. Don't hesitate to ask if you have some difficulties.
sections.grading:
Grading Scheme:
Problem Sets - 5%
2 Mid-terms - 25% each
Final Exam - 45%

You can skip up to 1 mid-term and your grading scheme will automatically become:
Problem Sets - 5%
Mid-term - 35%
Final Exam - 60%

Some statistics for the exams:
Mid-term 1
Mean: 87.52  SD: 8.03
Mid-term 2
Mean: 76.32  SD: 11.16
Final exam
Mean: 61.97  SD: 13.82

Got 95, 87.5 and 68 in the three exams respectively (+1 SD, +1 SD and +0.5 SD) and handed in all problem sets, overall score 83.5% and I got a B+. But one of my friends got just 1% below my overall score and got a B. I definitely won't say the grading is generous, but at least, acceptable.
sections.workload: You will have to do a problem set after covering 2 chapters. Totally 8 problem sets in the semester. The problem set basically comes from the exercises in the textbook. However, as long as you have submitted a word file on time - no matter what the content is, you would get full credits. You can just submit a file without a single word if you do not have time to do the assignments, but of course it's to your advantage to complete the problem sets.

sections.content: The content is not very difficult. Basically many topics are covered in DSE so it is quite relaxing and easy to follow at the beginning. Some topics like consumption possibilities,perfect competition and monopoly are quite difficult and very different from DSE so it is better to pay more attention to these chapters.If you can't follow, you may find the professor or TA immediately , they are willing to help. It 's better not to accumulate or leave your questions as you can't learn everything before exam.
sections.teaching: The explanation in lecture is very clear and adequate. But sometimes it is quite a rush in the lectures and it is difficult to follow, especially in some topics that are not taught in DSE. She will write some notes on the printed powerpoint slides so personally it is better to print out a copy of powerpoint and follow what she writes. Jotting notes in computer may be less efficient. Before midterms and final exam, she will give us some in-class exercise and MC questions which are generally easy and help us prepare for exam. Sometimes at the beginning of lectures she will share some videos which are quite funny. The TA guy will give us some exercises in tutorials but he is rushing everything super fast !!! If you have not attended lectures, basically you can't follow in tutorials after midterm 1.
sections.grading: The content is not difficult in this course so if you want to get a good grade, you may have to work hard and understand all the concepts thoroughly. There are two midterms and one final which are not difficult and the mean is quite high, like 8x% in the first midterm. The exam questions are very different from DSE one and at first it seems difficult as you are not familiar with the question type. However basically if you understand all the concepts thoroughly, attend all the lectures and tutorials and do the self-practices and problem sets, you will be doing fine in exam. Good grade comes with hard work. You can also earn some extra credits if you answer questions in lecture.

sections.content: Most of the syllabus content has already been covered in the IB/DSE, making the lectures very boring, and the tutorials useless. Furthermore, there is an alarming lack of use of higher-order skills in this course. By higher-order skills, I mean evaluation, synthesis, etc. This, again, has the effect of removing any potential challenge (if there was any to be had) from this course. Therefore, I think this course has no actual use, apart from helping students fulfill their requirements.
sections.teaching:
There is literally no interaction between the lecturer and the students. When the lecturer literally has to bribe the students to answer questions, it is obvious that the lecturer lacks ability to interact with students.

With regards to actual content, the lecturer is content with just reading from the powerpoint files that are on canvas. The only saving grace is that the lecturer explains how to do problems quite well.
sections.grading:
Overall, the grading system is excellent. This is because there are 2 marking schemes and the one with the higher mark is chosen. The difference between these 2 schemes is the different weights allocated to the midterm exams. Therefore, if you screw up one midterm, fear not.

As for the quizzes, students have an entire week to do one quiz, and there is no time limit for the quizzes. Students can also access any notes/lecture materials when doing the quiz, and so there is no actual difficulty. Quizzes are an excellent place to pick up marks.
sections.workload: The workload is nonexistent. There is no actual homework/assignments to do, apart from quizzes and problem sets. For more information regarding the quizzes, look at the 'Grading' section of this review.

However, again, I recommend that you go to class everyday to ensure that you understand the concepts in the professor's ways so that when you take the exams, professors will know that you have attended the lessons and you are ready with the material.

sections.teaching:
Professor Zhang definitely has a good voice which makes the lecture not so boring. Her teaching is based on the slides and the books, if you can understand the materials fully, there is not a great need to attend lectures.

In the lectures, she will project a printed slides and will keep making notes on it. Although most of them will not be tested in exam, you can get some extra knowledge. Her presentation is clear with identifiable accent, but with few value-added from the textbook. Breaks will be allowed in all lecture time, good for us to refresh our minds. She will also play different interesting videos during breaktime. Games related to microeconomics will be played in lectures, quite a good idea.

One point to note: never talk in her lectures, she will be annoyed and stop immediately if the lecture room is noisy.

Anyway there were just around half of the class attending each time.

Should be quite good, but final exam marks are not released

Around 1 sd to score an A range
